Mr. Subrata Saha. Advo. with Ms. Madhuri Saha. Adv., ------- For the petitioner. 
Mr. Ahmed Nowshed Jamil. Adv. With Ms. Syeda Shoukat Ara. Adv., --------- For the Opposite-Parties.
parties:
MD.AMIRUL ISLAM
Vs.
MD.SHAHABUDDIN AND OTHERS.
full_judgment:
1. The relevant facts necessary for disposal of the Rule as described in the revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure are that opposite party No.1 as pre-emptor instituted a suit under Section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption against the petitioner and others alleging inter alia that the case land originally belonged to Hazi Fazar Ali and R.O.R was correctly recorded and prepared in his name; Fazar Ali died leaving 3 sons namely Samsuddin Sarker, Shahabuddin and Alatab Ali to succeed him; shamsuddin died leaving defendant Nos.4-10 as his heirs to succeed him; Zinnatnnessa, daughter of Shamsuddin, died leaving defendant No.11 to succeed him; Altaf died leaving defendant No. 3 his widow and 2 brothers namely Shahabuddin (pre-emptor)and Shamsuddin; in this way defendant Nos. 2-11 became co-sharers in the case jote; defendant No.1 is a Stanger in the case jote; the pre-emptor on 25.02.1990 bought 12 decimals of land from the Joygunara, wife of defendant No. 5, by a registered sale deed ; defendant No. 1, in collusion with defendant N. 2, sold the case jote on 17.02.1991 by a registered sale deed ; after hearing about the sale the plaintiff came to the office of the Sub-Registrar and obtained a certified copy of the said deed of sale on 24.02.1991 and hence the case. 

 2. Defendant No. 1; contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations of the pre-emption petition and contended inter alia that Fazar Ali was the original owner of the suit land; he died leaving 3 sons and a widow to succeed him ; by amicable partition between the sons of deceased Fazar Ali, Shamsuddin got the case land measuring 73 decimals and 133 decimals other than the case land ; Shamsuddin Sarker sold the case land along with other lands to Hellal Udin; the plaintiff sold 65 decimals of land from the case jote along with other lands to Joynal Abedin and gave possession to him; C and B possesses the land of Khatian Nos. 308 and 321; Altab Ali gifted his portion of land to defendant No. 3 who is his daughter; Shamsuddin Sarker died leaving his wife, 3 sons and 4 daughters to succeed him; by amicable partition defendant No. 2 got 22 decimals of land; within the knowledge of the plaintiff, defendant No. 2 sold the said land by registered deed of sale dated 17.02.1991 plaintiff No. 1 executed a deed of re-conveyance in favour of defendant No. 2; that the plaintiff is well aware of the aforesaid deeds and he filed this case with oblique motives and as such the case is liable to be dismissed. 

 3. Defendant No. 2 also contested the suit by filing separate written statement denying all the materials of the pre-emption petition and contended inter alia that he firstly offered the plaintiff to purchase the case land and upon his refusal he sold the case land to defendant No.1 with an agreement re-conveyance and as such the suit is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed. 

 7. Mr. Subrata Saha with Ms.Madhuri Saha, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the pre-emptee petitioner submits that the pre-emptor has failed to prove by any cogent and reliable evidence that the impugned transfer is out and out sale, not a mortgage, the court of appeal below clearly erred in law to hold on surmises and conjectures that the transfer was indeed a sale and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that the learned trial Judge on consideration of the evidence on record , both oral and documentary, clearly found that the sale of the case land along with an agreement of re-conveyance is not a sale, but only a mortgage, the Judge of appeal below clearly erred in law in reversing the judgment of the trial Judge without setting aside these material findings with reference to evidence on record and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. He next submits that the deed of re-conveyance "Ext-B" was exhibited without any objection and the pre-emptor signally failed to produce a single witness to testify the authenticity of the deed of re-conveyance and moreover P.W. 2 stated in his examination-in-chief that he does not know whether there is any such deed of re-conveyance and whether the pre-emptor knew about the transfer of land, the Judge of appeal below erred in law in discarding the importance of "Exhibit-B" on mere surmise and conjectures and the same has occasioned failure of justice. He next added that regard being had to the fact that from the evidence of P.W. 1 and D.W. 2 the learned trial court clearly found that the pre-emptor was well aware of the transfer of land and the court of appeal below failed to consider at all this vital aspect of a pre-emption case and the same has occasioned failure of justice. He next added that in the plaint or even in their evidence the pre-emptor failed to give any exact date of his knowledge about the transfer of the case land and the court of appeal below totally failed to consider this vital aspect and the same has occasioned failure of justice. He finally submits that the learned Judge of appeal below as the final court of fact while reversing the judgment of the trial court totally ignored the evidence of the 5 witnesses examined by the contending parties in support of their respective cases and to consider the legal incidences that follows therefrom in clear violation of the provision of order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of Justice. 

 10. The submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners is of no substance since as per Section 95 (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 an usufructuary mortgage is required to be registered one. Admittedly the Kabala sought to be pre-empted was a sale deed. In the Kabala there is no stipulation for re-conveyance. The contention of the pre-emptees that the transfer sought to be pre-empted was not a sale but an usufructuary mortgage is based on an un-registered deed of agreement for re-conveyance. In the background of the facts of the case the Appellate Judge has observed that the alleged deed of re-conveyance was brought into existence upon an unholy alliance between the pre-emptees and the seller only to frustrate the claim of pre-emption. Since there was no registered deed of usufructuary mortgage in respect of the land sought to be pre-empted and that the deed of agreement for re-conveyance is an unregistered one, in my opinion the observation that has been made by the Appellate Court as to the nature of the deed of re-conveyance cannot be said to be of no basis. 

 19. The Judgment passed by learned Assistant Judge indicates that the learned Judge failed to notice the tenor of Section 95A and Section 96(10)(d) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Committed an error of law and by' the error the merit of the adjudication of the case had been seriously affected: Judgment perilously borders a perversity and legal infirmity. On the other hand, learned Sub-ordinate Judge as the Appellate Judge approached the debate in correct direction and reversing decision rendered by him is well founded and well merited. 

 21. On consideration of the impugned order it appears that decisions of facts reached by the Appellate Judge as last and final Judge of fact based on evidence and materials on record are not open to interference by the High Court in exercise of Revisional jurisdiction contemplated in section 115 of the Code unless it is shown that decisions are based upon gross misreading of evidence or those have been founded on misconception or misapplication or misapprehension of law or any misinterpretation of any material document or otherwise those are perverse being contrary to law, evidence and materials on record. Support for this proposition is sought to be drawn form a series of decisions both of our Jurisdiction and Foreign Jurisdiction. Durga Choudhrain Vs Jawahir Singh, 17 Indian Appeal 122, Nefar Chandra Pal Chowdhury Vs Shukkur Sheikh, AIR 1918 PC 92, Rahchandra Vs Ray Lingam, AIR 1963 SC 302. Fokruddin Mia and another vs Mohammad Khoda Baksu Sheikh, 29 DLR (SC) 268, Akrab Ali vs Zahiruddin , 30 DLR (SC) 81, Abdul Matin Chowdhury Vs Chapala Rani Sen and others, 37 DLR (AD) 205, Naimuddin Sarder Vs Md Abdul Kalam, 41 DLR (AD) 3, Naimuddin Kanchan Vs Ali Ashraf, 42 DLR (AD) 289, Mazharul Borhan Vs Ah Bhuiyan, 1995 BLD (AD) 237, Uaider Unnessa and another Vs Monowara Begum and others, 1996 BLD (AD) 280, Federal Radid Commission Vs Nelson Brothers Board and Electric and Power Company Vs National Relations Board, (1942) US 533, Gujt Heluering, Commissioner of International Revenue Vs John Kehoc, (1939) 309 US 267 and State of New York and others Vs United States of America (1946) 331 US 284 are some of the authorities which may be profitably noticed. A study of the decisions rendered, reason assigned in rendering decisions and conclusions reached by Appellate Judge does not come into sight that there had been misreading of evidence or those had been founded on any misconception, misapplication and misapprehension of law or mis-interpretation of any material document or otherwise those were wrong-headed. On bestowing my anxious and dispassionate consideration and thought and having also taken into account of all the pros and cons of the matter and the catena of authorities pronounced by Superior Courts of our Jurisdiction and also of foreign Jurisdiction, I am of the conviction that this Rule arising out of Civil Revision Petition is bereft of any substance and the same must be discharged. The case referred by Mr. Ahmed Nawshed Jamil the learned Advocate for the opposite party Reported in 10 BLC P-603 is squarely applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case.
